claims.text: Conventional TOR-TILD EAM references inadequately represent the configurational diversity of multicomponent alloy liquids.
A deep-learning potential can be trained on ab initio configurations.
The training set should extensively sample liquid configurations over 0.9–1.1 times the melting temperature.
The proposed machine-learned potential is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting.
Including a large variety of ab initio configurations improves representation of diverse local atomic environments.
The deep-learning potential encapsulates the many-body interactions relevant to the alloy liquid.
The expanded liquid training set bridges the representation gap between conventional EAM references and the ab initio liquid.
The trained potential captures complex and nonlocal liquid-state energy landscapes.
A liquid-trained machine-learned reference will sample configurations that overlap better with the target ab initio liquid than an EAM reference.
Better reference–target phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The intervention will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 50–100 meV/atom relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will improve free-energy accuracy.
The proposed improvement may not extend to temperatures significantly below melting.
The proposed improvement may not transfer to alloys whose chemical interactions differ substantially from those represented in the training data.
Elemental and binary free-energy benchmarks provide evidence that machine-learned potentials capture complex interactions.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction depends on training-data quality and alloy composition.
